title: Binary reduced Vandermonde matrix
statement: For natural numbers $k,n$ and a positive extension degree $\ell$, let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ be elements of the binary extension field of degree $\ell$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Define a matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with $n$ columns and $(\lfloor k/2\rfloor\ell+1)$ rows: its first row is constant $1$, and its remaining rows are the binary coordinates of the odd powers $\alpha_j^{2q+1}$, for each applicable exponent index $q$ and each coordinate in the extension field representation.
hypotheses_covered: $\alpha$ assigns an element of the degree-$\ell$ binary extension field to each of the $n$ column indices
caveat: The formal statement relies on an upstream row equivalence and encoding whose precise indexing and coordinate convention are not included in the supplied definitions.
